stimulus.source_note: Woodcut of Potosi from Pedro Cieza de Leon, Cronica del Peru, 1553, public domain.
stimulus.text: The woodcut, printed in Pedro Cieza de Leon's Chronicle of Peru in 1553, shows the Cerro de Potosi, the great silver mountain, rising over the mining town below. The slopes are labeled with the names of the ore veins, and the town at the foot of the mountain holds churches and houses. Workers climb the paths up the mountain.

parts.prompt: Identify what the woodcut shows about Potosi.
Explain how the image shows the importance of silver to the Spanish Empire.
Explain one way the woodcut's date, 1553, matters for using it as evidence.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
